newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- GEORGE WARNS ON RISING DOMESTIC SPENDING

Bank of England governor Eddie George has warned that domestic spending is rising at an unsustainable rate, after a recent survey showed shortages of skilled labour had driven up service sector wages. George said interest rates should rise to slow the upswing and prevent further inflation.
-- CU BACKS DOWN ON PLAN TO DENY VOTES TO REPORT

Insurance group Commercial Union has backed down on its proposal to deny investors the right to vote on its report and accounts, only a day after the proposal was first announced. The proposal was widely criticized, and CU was threatened with an attempt to oust its chief executive John Carter.
-- FORMER SHIPPING GROUP CHIEF GUILTY OF 1.2 BILLION DOLLAR
BCCI FRAUD
Former chairman of the Gulf Group shipping empire, Abbas Gokal, has been convicted of a 1.2 billion dollar fraud, the largest single fraud in British history. He will be sentenced May 6.
-- S KOREAN CAMPAIGN ANGERS BRUSSELS

The European Union has threatened to refer South Korea's "frugality" campaign to the World Trade Organization, claiming it consisted of an attempt at non-tariff barriers against foreign consumer products. Seoul has argued that the anti-import campaign against luxury products was led by citizen-led groups, not the government, and its finance and commerce minister has stated he is opposed to the campaign. Korea has until May 15 to act.
-- BAe AND LOCKHEED LINK ON ARMY VEHICLE BID

British Aerospace has joined up with US group Lockheed Martin for a 5 billion dollar contract to supply British and US armies with battlefield reconnaissance vehicles. The link is seen as a step forward in UK and US defence relations and will bring electronic specialists and armoured vehicle makers together. The alliance may be opposed by a team which includes GKN Defence and GEC-Marconi.
-- BANK CHIEF WARNING OVER EMU TIMETABLE

According to Eddie George, governor of the Bank of England, attempts to force the Emu to adhere to a timetable rather than economic criteria would be dangerous. He added no one should want to join a union unless they had been convinced economic risks were minimal and stressed the UK remained committed to monetary and fiscal stability as demanded by the Maastricht treaty.
-- ONE THIRD OF STAFF TO GO AT UNITED ASSURANCE

Home services insurer United Assurance will shed one-third of its staff and cut its number of branches from 279 to 116, in an attempt to save 37 million stg a year. George Mack, company CEO said the cuts were "essential in enabling us to compete in our chosen markets and increase sales." The group, which was formed in the merger between Refuge Group and United Friendly, hope to have a harmonised product range beginning in August.
-- ALPHA OMIKRON QUITS AIM AS ADVISER RESIGNS

Alpha Omikron has become the third company to be expelled from junior stockmarket Aim, after its nominated adviser (nomad) resigned and they failed to find a replacement. All Aim-listed companies are expected to have a nomad, and once it resigns shares are suspended for a month until the company finds a replacement. The stock exchange said it has no problem with the way Aim operates and has no plans to amend the rules.
-- ING PLANS ACQUISITIONS TO PREPARE FOR SINGLE CURRENCY

Dutch Financial group ING, owner of UK's Barings, is seeking acquisitions in European investment banking to aid position itself for the arrival of Emu. ING's annual report will detail to its shareholders its plans to play a significant role in Emu, which it will achieve through organic growth and strategic alliances. It will focus on employee benefits, corporate finance, treasury, clearing and asset management.
-- VODAFONE GSM USERS SET TO RECEIVE E-MAIL

Shares in Internet services provider Internet Technology Group (ITG) rose 5p to 70p on Thursday following news of an agreement with Vodata, a subsidiary of mobile phone operator Vodafone. The deal means that users of Vodafone GSM mobile phones will be able to receive e-mail directly to their sets. For a full range of news monitoring services, phone BMC +44-171-377-1742
